sermons.title: LIVE: Through the Bible with Andrew Wommack - Part 2 - June 15, 2026
summary: The sermon emphasizes that believers possess the same resurrection power of Christ within them and must understand their true identity as redeemed, righteous, and whole in Christ rather than broken or condemned.
Jesus teaches that life is not about accumulating possessions or fearing people's judgment, but about seeking God's kingdom first and trusting Him to provide all necessary things.

The pastor warns against hypocrisy, covetousness, and anxious thoughts about material needs, urging believers to recognize they are stewards of God's resources meant to bless others, not hoarders focused on self-preservation.

sermons.title: LIVE Through the Bible with Andrew Wommack - June 5, 2026
summary: Jesus asks his disciples who they believe he is, and Peter's confession that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of the living God, comes through divine revelation rather than human reasoning.
Jesus teaches that following him requires denying oneself, taking up one's cross, and being willing to lose one's life for his sake, which paradoxically leads to finding true life.
The sermon emphasizes that Satan can speak through even well-intentioned people, and believers must recognize and reject lies that contradict God's word and purpose.

sermons.title: LIVE: Through the Bible with Andrew Wommack - June 12, 2026
summary: Jesus heals a man born blind on the Sabbath, demonstrating that miracles transcend human tradition and religious law, and that faith requires both belief and obedient action.
The blind man's simple testimony—'I was blind, now I see'—proves more powerful than the Pharisees' theological arguments, showing that personal experience of God's power cannot be argued away.
The passage challenges believers to prioritize God's truth over human approval, to recognize that miracles still happen today, and to understand that faith without works is dead.

sermons.title: Lessons from David: Episode 1
summary: Saul's disobedience in offering a sacrifice he was forbidden to make cost him the kingdom, demonstrating that circumstances cannot justify violating God's commands.
The pastor emphasizes learning from biblical characters' mistakes rather than repeating them, using Saul's people-pleasing nature and fear of man as a cautionary example.
God's search for a man after His own heart—David—was initiated because of Saul's failure to obey, showing that disobedience has generational consequences.

sermons.title: Healing Journeys: Episode 29
summary: God has already provided healing through Christ's stripes, and believers must take their God-given authority to command sickness to leave rather than begging God to heal them.
The power of spoken words aligned with God's authority is essential—believers must speak directly to their problems, not to God about their problems, following Jesus's teaching to speak to mountains.

Multiple testimonies demonstrate that when people stand in faith, speak with authority over their conditions, and refuse to accept the devil's lies, miraculous healings manifest immediately and permanently.
